a1
Jacob reached a well in the open country, where shepherds waited to roll away its great stone.
a2
They said: here comes Laban's daughter Rachel, with his sheep.
a3
Jacob rolled the stone away, watered her flock, kissed Rachel, and wept aloud.
b1
Laban welcomed him. Jacob said: I will work seven years for Rachel, your younger daughter.
b2
The seven years felt like a few days, because he loved her.
c1
But on the wedding night, Laban brought his older daughter Leah to Jacob.
c2
In the morning Jacob cried: why did you deceive me? Laban said: the younger is never given before the firstborn.
c3
After that bridal week, Laban gave him Rachel too, for seven more years of work.
d1
The Lord saw that Leah was unloved, and she bore Reuben, Simeon, and Levi.
d2
Her fourth son she named Judah: this time I will praise the Lord.
h1
Leah was the wife Jacob had not chosen, and the Lord saw that she was unloved.
h2
Her story moves from longing to praise.
h3
You are not defined by who chose you. God sees you, and he has chosen you.
h4
Today, bring your longing to God.
i
Where do you feel unchosen? What does God say?
